answer.reason: The packet establishes that the existing assertion would abort if the document URL copy encounters an injected allocation failure. It does not establish that a valid fuzz input produces a document with a non-NULL doc->URL or that the copy reaches the injected allocator under the supplied build. The finite target execution is therefore unproved.

scope_contract.reason: The old entry calls xmlXIncludeProcessNode and checks its context error code. That operation delegates to the document URL copy.

feasible_trigger.reason: The harness can supply a URL and select an allocation index, but the supplied parser code does not show that the parsed document receives doc->URL. The supplied xmlStrdup body delegates to an unread xmlStrndup body. The relevant build defaults are also unread.

observable_consequence.reason: Conditional on that copy failing through the injected allocator, the new memory reporter updates no XInclude context error field. The context starts with errNo zero, the getter returns that field, and the existing assertion aborts on a mismatch.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: For this conditional URL-copy failure, root processing returns before include traversal. The existing check uses neither ProcessNode's return nor the global last error; later operations follow the check.

identity_preserved.reason: The before and after evidence concerns the same root URL-copy failure and the same old harness check. The removed reporter set ctxt->errNo; the added reporter does not. This supports a conditional change in outcome, although trigger feasibility remains unknown.

citations.dependency_reason: Fuzz input supplies the main URL and entity.
The parser forwards the supplied URL.
The parser copies the URL to the input filename, which does not itself prove doc->URL is set.
The URL copy delegates to xmlStrndup, whose allocation behavior is not supplied.
A selected allocator call can set the failure flag.
A NULL error pointer leaves any context error object untouched; the reporter updates the global error.
The existing check aborts when the failure flag differs from its expected value.
The reporter's global error is a separate indication that the existing check does not read.
